scope: Exact current registry-test repair separating historical Pentateuch comparison replay from the deliberately stale live-canonical snapshot check; not a change to frozen validator, source evidence or canonical text

failure_review.failure: test_current_registry expected an empty error list, but the frozen Pentateuch comparison returned GEN.4.8.speech: canonical baseline drift
failure_review.cause: The comparison pins the complete preapplication YAML bytes. A valid note-only change still stales that historical canonical snapshot.

review_rationale: Live registry, coverage, Samuel comparison and source-selection checks remain outside the Genesis historical overlay. The renamed test no longer mislabels historical Pentateuch validation as live validation.

A separately named historical test uses the already reviewed Genesis-only guarded baseline view, asserts the historical target bytes while inside it, and verifies restoration of actual current bytes afterward.

A separate direct live test requires exact current candidate bytes and the exact one-element stale-snapshot error list. It does not filter away the error or claim the current standalone validator succeeds.

The deliberately corrupted GEN baseline-hash test first requires a clean historical result and then the exact targeted error, preventing the already-stale live snapshot from making the negative test pass vacuously.

Unknown current Genesis bytes are rejected before historical replay, and an unrelated Exodus30:6 byte mutation remains visible under the Genesis-only overlay. These checks establish the repair is narrowly scoped.

The original integration gap is retained as a real newly discovered dependency. The 28 implementation tests and13 postapplication tests did not establish full repository compatibility; this separate review does not revise those frozen judgments.
